item.title: Barcelona superstar to miss Spain’s Czech Republic match after suffering knee discomfort against Atletico Madrid
item.description: Barcelona superstar to miss Spain’s Czech Republic match after suffering knee discomfort against Atletico Madrid Barcelona have been handed a fitness concern after Lamine Yamal reported discomfort in his right knee following their 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid . As a result, according to Mundo Deportivo , the forward will remain in Barcelona rather than travel with Spain for Thursday’s Nations League fixture against the Czech Republic, with his availability for the meeting with England on November 15 still dependent on his recovery. The outlet mentions that Yamal underwent medical tests after Sunday’s match at the Metropolitano, and the decision was taken for him to continue his recovery in Barcelona. Indeed, the Spanish international is expected to join Luis de la Fuente’s squad in the coming days, but his participation against England cannot yet be considered certain. Yamal to miss Spain’s trip to face Czech Republic Spain are scheduled to face the Czech Republic in Prague on November 12 before hosting England at the Metropolitano three days later. Lamine Yamal suffered knee discomfort vs Atletico Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Yamal is expected to miss the first fixture as Barcelona and the national team’s medical staff monitor his condition. The forward was the only Barcelona international to return to the club immediately after the victory over Atletico, while his teammates remained in Madrid ahead of their international commitments. For now, the Royal Spanish Football Federation’s medical department is maintaining contact with Barcelona’s doctors to follow the progress of the affected players. Understandably, the priority will be to assess the 19-year-old’s recovery before deciding whether he can join the national team group and feature in the second fixture. Flick faces another concern over Yamal’s workload The situation is an unwelcome development for Hansi Flick, particularly after Yamal played an important role in Barcelona’s victory against Atletico. Lamine Yamal will miss Spain’s next match vs Czech Republic. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The teenager provided the assist for Fermin Lopez’s decisive goal in the 66th minute, helping the Catalans secure three valuable points. Flick had already highlighted the difficulty of managing players’ workloads during international breaks , with several Barcelona regulars leaving to represent their countries. “It’s part of our job: there’s an international break now, and the Spanish players are usually not here during those breaks. “Managing playing time is crucial. It’s important that they do the same with their national teams,” he noted. As a result of the aforementioned development, the immediate concern will be to ensure that Yamal does not aggravate the discomfort while travelling or returning to competitive action too soon, something that Barcelona learned the hard way through Raphinha’s recent problems.

Villegas’ coach and husband, Ali Taktak, said the person who provided the information about Coelho’s PMMA injections also identified the clinic and doctor where she allegedly got them in Brazil — Fernando Vitor at the Instituto Lappidare. Current champion Coelho declined to confirm or deny allegation USA TODAY Sports confirmed the person who provided this information to Villegas is a licensed health professional in Brazil and that Coelho appeared at this clinic with Vitor, according to a video on Instagram . Vitor and his clinic have financial ties to the sport’s governing body through Tamer El-Guindy , a promoter of bodybuilding events and producer at the Olympia event. Coelho, who grew up in Brazil, hasn’t denied or confirmed whether she received PMMA injections. Cicherillo asked Coelho about the controversy at a public seminar in September . “If I get into that, I’m not doing any good for the sport,” Coelho said. Coelho didn’t return several messages seeking additional comment. Vitor and El-Guindy also didn’t’ return messages. The organization and its president Jim Manion also did not return several messages seeking comment by phone and email. Nor did Jake Wood, owner of the Olympia event, the top event in the sport. After Villegas received this information about Coelho last year, Villegas said her coach, Taktak, shared it with league leadership. In response, Villegas said the IFBB Pro League stated it “has no rules prohibiting PMMA plastic muscle implants” and that “no one is asked to submit a resume of what they did to attain their physique before stepping on stage.” This response echoed top personalities in the sport who criticized Villegas for speaking out. Cicherillo has called Villegas' allegations "very unprofessional." “We don't have any rules set forth and we don't have any testing procedures,” Cicherillo said on a podcast last yea r after Villegas spoke out against Coelho. “This is anything but a 'natural' federation." Ray agreed. Even if Coelho did use PMMA, "What rule would she be breaking?" Ray asked. "If you can find the rule book, what rule book is she breaking?... So where does Sarah have a foot to stand on?" Worse, Murray has failed to leverage the Vikings' best player, perennial Pro Bowler Justin Jefferson, who's as talented as any wideout in the league but is averaging fewer than five receptions and 60 receiving yards per game in 2026. "They've got nowhere to go. I don't see Kyler getting better and resurrecting his career. Way too inconsistent, doesn't anticipate well," former New York Giants vice president of player personnel Marc Ross told USA TODAY Sports. "And Kevin O'Connell hasn't really shown any ability to help Murray out to this point." O'Connell, who has a reputation as a quarterback whisperer, bemoaned the lack of offensive execution after last week's 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions, Minnesota's first of the season. He's also noted that the team has been in the shotgun formation a lot more this season, which is Murray's preference, though that's probably come at the expense of running the ball more effectively − and it hasn't helped get Jefferson sufficiently involved, either. "I thought there were some play-pass chances that we didn't see or didn't pull the trigger on," O'Connell said after the loss at Ford Field, when Murray connected five times with Jefferson for just 33 yards, though one hook-up did produce a TD. "We know how much (Jefferson) impacts the game, so it's going to be something we'll continue to emphasize and continue to try to do both in rhythm on the scheduled timing of the play and then some of the off-schedule opportunities as well. "(Murray is) in the gun a lot. We're marrying that up as creatively and as effectively as we can. ... So, I think it's just continuing to build that rapport of the plans, the comfort level, continuing to implore some input from him on things he likes and (saying), ‘Hey, how can we carve it and make it even more cleaner and better for him?’ so that we do get some of that comfort where he'll throw things with anticipation, and we get to look for a play. We all know it's coming." Is Carson Wentz the Vikings' QB answer? But is it coming? Six games into his Minnesota career, Murray's 86.6 passer rating ranked 20th in the NFL and lagged about five points behind the league average. In terms of ESPN's QBR metric, his 44.6 figure ranks 26th. And his 170.3 passing yards per game? The lowest figure of his NFL career. "Kyler just doesn't look as if he any confidence or feel flow," said Ross, now an NFL Network analyst. "The defense is good enough to win the whole damn thing, but they have to hold everyone to 13 points. If they can just get anything from the offense …" A big if, but one the Vikings can now assess freshly with Wentz, who helped lead Minnesota to wins in the first two games of the season after Murray was concussed in the first quarter of the opener. And while O'Connell said last week he remains committed to Murray as his starter, he also spelled out what he expects Wentz to provide against Buffalo. "He’s going to throw a lot of completions. He’s going to put the ball in play. He’s got such a high, high understanding of not only the offense, but what he’s looking at on the other side. He’s got 100 games of experience," O'Connell said of Wentz, the No. 2 pick of the 2016 draft who put the Philadelphia Eagles on the path to their first Super Bowl victory but went down with a knee injury late in the 2017 season. Knowing where his bread is buttered − as well as signaling internal locker room frustration − Wentz admitted he plans to feed Jefferson on Monday. Frequently. "Just get him the rock. I mean, he's as good as I've been around," Wentz said of Jefferson, who's averaging more than 30 yards fewer than his career average of 88.2 receiving yards per game, the second-highest figure in NFL history. "And so, for him, the last couple of weeks maybe not getting it as much as he would maybe want − I get it, I'd be frustrated if I were him." Said Hall of Fame receiver and Vikings legend Randy Moss on ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown" on Sunday morning, in a nod to Jefferson: "Whoever the quarterback is, I need you to heat my franchise player up." That was once the role of J.J. McCarthy, whom former Minnesota GM Kwesi Adofo-Mensah moved up to draft 10th overall in 2024. But O'Connell quickly − prematurely? − declared Murray the winner of the team's QB competition on Aug. 11, during the very early stages of training camp. Rookie GM Nolan Teasley wasted little time offloading McCarthy, who was traded to the Giants for a mere fifth-round pick on September 28 but has now won both starts with his new team. And McCarthy sounded like a man thankful to be liberated, whether or not he should have been, from Minnesota after taking over as New York's starter going into Week 7, when he ultimately engineered an upset of the Texans in Houston. "Everything about this place it feels very fitting for me," McCarthy said of the Giants' culture, players and coaches. item.title: ‘I’m very grateful for the city of Indianapolis’: Jonathan Taylor delivers apparent goodbye to Colts
item.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) waves to fans as he leaves the field Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, after losing a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. The Indianapolis Colts’ season continued to go in the wrong direction on Sunday with a 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys as the team lost its fifth consecutive game. With the trade deadline just days away, Jonathan Taylor sounded like a player who knows his time in Indianapolis could be coming to an end. Speaking after the game, the star running back didn’t commit to the Colts or shoot down the trade rumors. Instead, Taylor thanked the city and its fans, saying that if Sunday was his final game with the team, he’s “very grateful” for his time there. Colts’ Fire Sale The Colts have fallen apart this season, dropping to 2-7 after Sunday’s loss. The team fired general manager Chris Ballard in October and has already traded away veteran leaders Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner for draft picks. Taylor, a three-time Pro Bowler who won the NFL rushing title in 2021, has reportedly drawn interest from multiple teams ahead of Tuesday’s 4 p.m. ET deadline. But there have been plenty of twists in the trade talks. Before Sunday’s game, Fox’s Jay Glazer reported that the New York Giants pulled their trade offer for Taylor, according to OutKick. The Giants had reportedly offered a package built around second- and fifth-round picks, but they backed off after the Colts held out for a first-rounder. Other contenders, including the Denver Broncos and Cincinnati Bengals, are reportedly still lurking. Taylor is under contract through 2028, which gives Indianapolis plenty of leverage to hold firm on its asking price. ‘Very grateful’ After the loss to Dallas, Taylor was asked about the possibility of being traded, and he didn’t stick to the usual script. “I think you play every game like it’s your last, but at the end of the day this has been a spot where I grew up,” Taylor said after the game . “I think I mentioned this to you guys, like you go to college, you’re a young man, but you really grew up, you started a family and you really embraced this city, the people, and you’re just like…” “This place helped shape me into the man I am today. If it is [my last game], I’m very grateful for the city of Indianapolis,” he continued. Taylor also made sure to thank Colts fans for their support over the years. “I just hope that they appreciate and know that I appreciate them and it was a pleasure to put on display not only my hard work but the team’s hard work each and every single week, each and every single year. Just know it was a pleasure,” Taylor said. Needless to say, it certainly sounded like a goodbye. item.title: Ashley Young makes concerning Senne Lammens claim after Aston Villa disasterclass
item.description: Ashley Young makes concerning Senne Lammens claim after Aston Villa disasterclass Former Manchester United captain Ashley Young has seemingly questioned the mentality of goalkeeper Senne Lammens following his poor performance in the draw with Aston Villa. Senne Lammens Horror show Lammens endured a game to forget as United and Villa played out a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford on Sunday. He was culpable for both of Villa’s quickfire goals. The first squirmed between his legs from Alysson’s shot, and he then parried another Alysson effort into the path of the in-form Nicolas Jackson, who tapped in from close range to hand the visitors a commanding two-goal cushion. Beyond his two mistakes, Lammens repeatedly hesitated to come off his line to clear the danger, placing United at risk. The Belgium international also did not cover himself in glory for Leon Goretzka’s finish. Fortunately for United, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu came off the bench to score in stoppage time, making it 4-4 and ensuring the points were shared. Nevertheless, the Red Devils remain 18th in the Premier League and are guaranteed to occupy a place in the relegation zone for at least two weeks as the international break proceeds. Lammens’ disastrous performance was merely the latest and most damning in a growing list of displays that have left a great deal to be desired this season. Speaking on Sky Sports , Young claimed that Lammens has simply not been the same since his costly error at the World Cup with Belgium. Young’s claim The former United captain said [via Football 365 ], “For me, on the goal, Diogo Dalot, you have got to defend your goal. Slide in. Slide in. He is going in with his opposite foot.” “And then the goalkeeper doesn’t do himself any glory here.” He added, “You know, I think since the World Cup, he made that mistake, and he hasn’t looked the same as last season.” Roy Keane also stated, “Nightmare start for Utd. Obviously, never got going. Villa looked sharp. Again, the set piece, nice layoff, shot on target. The keeper has got to do better.” “And like all top strikers, you look at the reaction. He is on the move again, poor from Utd. The goalkeeper – standard save.” United are next in action on November 22 when they go away to Liverpool. item.title: Nuggets list six key players including Nikola Jokic on injury list after getting stuck in Mexico City
item.description: Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post The Denver Nuggets are heading into a marquee Western Conference clash with major weaknesses after logistical travel issues on their way back from the 2026 NBA Mexico City Games. The Nuggets picked up a 114-102 win over the Indiana Pacers in Mexico City, one of three international regular season games played by the NBA this season. Unfortunately, the situation the Nuggets have found themselves in since the end of that game highlight how the slightest disruption during these international games can cause major issues to the routines of high-level NBA players. Nuggets get stuck in Mexico City and face major disruption before next game The Nuggets had to spend an extra 24 hours in Mexico City after their win over the Pacers on November 8 due to a number of travel issues and arrive for their road game in Houston with less than 24 hours before the game, listing most core players as questionable because of the situation . “The Nuggets have had major plane delays getting out of Mexico City, per sources, but hopeful to get out tonight. They are listing Nikola Jokic, Jamal Murray, Aaron Gordon, Cam Johnson, Christian Braun and DeMar DeRozan questionable tomorrow in Houston for various minor ailments.” Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon, and Nikola Jokic are the starting five of the Nuggets while DeMar DeRozan has been their sixth man off the bench all season. Jokic is averaging 22.9 points, 10.1 rebounds and 9.1 assists this season, and his absence would be a huge blow to the 5-3 Nuggets in a big-time clash against the 7-3 Rockets. Instead of risking their core players on the court against a physical Rockets side, the Nuggets might play the long game and give their stars the rest they need instead of risking injury due to fatigue and poor recovery from two interrupted days due to travel issues. The Nuggets flight could not leave Mexico City due to an issue with the plane’s door , with the team boarding the plane at 9:00 p.m.and sat in their seats till 3:25 a.m. before being told that they could not fly that night due to the aforementioned door issue. The Nuggets landed in Houston around 6:30 p.m. local time, which is roughly 24 hours before tip-off against the Rockets, giving the players just one evening of rest before playing with no practice since before their Mexico City game. item.title: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash
item.description: Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images Mike Tomlin is expecting a blockbuster AFC North showdown between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals, backing both teams to deliver an entertaining contest with the division lead at stake. The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. Mike Tomlin backs Steelers pass rush to challenge Joe Burrow and Cincinnati Bengals Tomlin made no secret of his excitement when discussing the matchup, admitting he would be more than happy to make the trip to Cincinnati. “It’s AFC North football and you know I love that. You can airmail me right to Cincinnati,” Tomlin said. He also highlighted the individual battle that could define the game, with Joe Burrow and the Bengals passing attack facing Pittsburgh’s formidable pass rush. “It’s good on good. Joe Burrow and that Cincinnati passing game vs T.J. Watt and the four-man rush of the Steelers…. Bring your popcorn and get your cameras ready.” Pittsburgh will arrive with plenty of confidence after enjoying a bye week. The Steelers’ four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. Tomlin will have a particularly interesting perspective from the NBC booth as he watches the Steelers take on a Bengals team that will be determined to settle the score on home turf. item.title: Oscar Piastri splits with Mark Webber after disappointing F1 season
item.description: Oscar Piastri has split from manager and former Formula 1 driver Mark Webber as he seeks a new direction for 2027 and beyond. Piastri, 25, has been mentored by nine-time race winner and Australian compatriot Webber since his emergence as a top prospect in junior formula and, most famously, Webber negotiated Piastri’s move to McLaren for the 2023 season, despite a tense stand-off with Alpine in the summer of 2022. Piastri was the F1 championship leader throughout most of the 2025 campaign before falling away in the final rounds, eventually finishing third, 13 points off champion and McLaren teammate Lando Norris . However, Webber has taken more of a back seat with Piastri this season, moving to a “behind the scenes” role as opposed to being ever-present at the racetrack. And Piastri has endured a tough campaign, failing to win a race and he currently sits a distant seventh in the standings, 94 points behind Norris. A statement on Monday from Webber confirmed that his partnership with Piastri has now ended. "Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close," said Webber, in conjunction with his partner Ann Webber. "This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure, and for us to embark on our new ventures. Piastri trails Lando Norris by 94 points this season (Getty) "We wish Oscar all the very best for a long and successful career." Piastri added: "I'd like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. "Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward." Piastri’s new management structure going into the 2027 season is yet to be confirmed.

item.title: Slegers hails ‘world class’ Arsenal duo after beating Liverpool
item.description: Slegers hails ‘world class’ Arsenal duo after beating Liverpool Arsenal Women boss Renée Slegers praised Emily Fox’s attacking contribution after the full-back played a key role in both goals during the 2-1 win over Liverpool. Both of Arsenal’s goals came from deliveries from the right, with Fox and Lisa Baum providing crosses for Alessia Russo to convert. “We have world-class full-backs and we ask them to do different things for us,” Slegers said after the victory. “Sometimes it’s wide to get crosses in, sometimes it’s going inside to combine. “I thought Emily Fox was outstanding today.” Slegers was also delighted with Russo’s movement and finishing after the striker scored twice to secure the victory. “The two goals that Alessia scored, they’re so good,” she added. “She picks up good positions in the box, the finishes are so clean. “Really happy with the two goals.”

item.title: Beckham tries to recruit Dybala to Inter Miami
item.description: Beckham tries to recruit Dybala to Inter Miami Paulo Dybala’s future may lie far from Roma and Serie A. The Argentine striker, currently sidelined with a muscle injury, has reportedly been targeted by two Major League Soccer clubs. Among the most likely destinations is David Beckham’s Inter Miami, a club that also hosts Lionel Messi and Rodrigo De Paul. This prospect could open up new horizons for the Giallorossi’s number 21, whose contract remains a key issue in the coming months. According to Radio Manà Manà , Beckham has already initiated initial contact with Dybala’s entourage to gauge the player’s willingness to move to the United States at the end of the season. The prospect of joining Messi in Florida would not be unwelcome to the Argentine, who may be considering a new professional experience after his years in the Italian league. New York City is also said to be pursuing him.

White responded by posting an image of himself at the White House podium with the caption “On to the next chapter,” and he later said he was flying to Washington, D.C., to meet with Trump on Monday. But on Sunday, Trump told reporters that he was “only kidding” about the offer, though he added that some people thought it was “actually a pretty good idea” and that White was still coming to see him. White’s ties to Trump go back decades, and he has spoken at the last three Republican National Conventions. But after Trump’s 2024 election win, White insisted he was done with politics. “I’m never f***ing doing this again,” White told The New Yorker . “I want nothing to do with this s***. It’s gross. Following a disappointing 31-13 loss to Alabama, questions are growing about whether the Tigers made the right decision in pursuing the head coach. ESPN analyst Scott Van Pelt has questioned the hype and investment the team made on Kiffin. During an appearance on ‘SVPod,’ Van Pelt pointed to LSU’s three losses and suggested the program’s pursuit of Kiffin was driven by expectations that have yet to translate into results on the field. “You guys were chasing him like he was Nick Saban. They’ve already got three losses, man,” Van Pelt said. The analyst also questioned what LSU could point to as a major achievement so far in Kiffin’s tenure as the Tigers struggled against some of their toughest opponents. Van Pelt acknowledged that LSU still has significant opportunities ahead, with upcoming matchups against Texas and Tennessee. However, he argued that the Tigers have not shown enough to justify the expectations surrounding Kiffin’s arrival. “To date, what’s your win? What are you hanging your hat on? Who are you pointing at and going, ‘Huh? See what we did against Clemson, A&M, McNeese?’ What do you got? Nothing. Nothing,” Van Pelt said. item.title: ‘On his side’ – Jaylen Brown’s blunt answer about potential conversation with Jayson Tatum
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images Even after the dust around his trade has settled, Jaylen Brown isn’t willing to engage with his former Boston Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum. Tatum and Brown played together for nine years, reaching five Eastern Conference Finals, two NBA Finals, and winning an NBA Championship in 2024. The All-NBA pair was considered one of the best in the league, but Brown’s departure from the Celtics has exposed just how frail their relationship was over their nine-year stint together. Jaylen Brown claims he won’t speak to Jayson Tatum before 76ers vs. Celtics game Speaking to reporters after the Philadelphia 76ers beat the Chicago Bulls, Jaylen Brown was asked about facing the Boston Celtics for the first time, and how he plans to reunite with Jayson Tatum. Brown suggested he still hasn’t spoken with Tatum since his departure, and has no reason or interest in speaking with his former All-Star teammate. Brown curtly said: “Nope (when asked if he and Jayson Tatum had talked since NBA Media Day). There’s nothing to talk about. He’s on his side, and I’m on my side playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win, so there’s nothing to talk about. Check the ball up. “I love Boston. Boston is a great city. A lot of great people I’ve developed relationships with. I’m just focused on what is in front of me right now. That’s the most important thing…” Brown has made his issues with Tatum and the Celtics no secret, even if he hasn’t openly discussed what exactly went wrong between the two. At one point, Brown and Tatum appeared to be good friends, with their on-court chemistry reflecting that very well. But the pair clearly have some unresolved issues and will try to get the better of each other when the 76ers face the Celtics this week. item.description: Neither Kentucky nor Florida will feel good coming into this one. Kentucky dropped a stinker in Knoxville, losing 34-6, while Florida got whipped by Oklahoma in The Swamp, 23-7. Kentucky rolled to a 38-7 victory. But both coaches are different, and I am not so sure a blowout is in the cards this year for either side. Both teams will look to right the ship and prevent one loss from becoming two. You better believe Jon Sumrall and Brad White will be coming back to Lexington with a win on their mind, while Kentucky will be looking to take the awful sting of that Volunteer loss out of their system while also keeping their College Football Playoff hopes afloat. Florida Gators (5-4, 3-4) Florida is a shockingly inconsistent team. The Gators destroyed Ole Miss by 24, knocked off Texas by 3, but lost by 28 to Missouri and 16 to Oklahoma. But just a game before, Aaron Philo started 5-of-7, but those two incompletions were interceptions, and he was benched before halftime. Where the Gators go from there is anyone’s guess, but Kentucky will need to prepare to see both guys. On defense, Florida is just as volatile. 425.3 total yards per game is what they give up for the year, but in the last 3 games, they have surrendered 278 yards to Texas, 318 to Georgia, and 351 to Oklahoma. So, Brad White has got his side playing a little better. But it really comes down to which team shows up. Will it be the team that knocked off Texas or the team that lost at home to Oklahoma? item.title: Bronny James Claps Back At Pistons Fan: “How Much Money You Make A Year?”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Bronny James didn’t feature in the Los Angeles Lakers ‘ 121-116 win over the Detroit Pistons at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday, but he still ended up making headlines. Bronny had some choice words for a Pistons fan during the game, as he appeared to get into a back-and-forth with one of them. “Can you run a mile?” Bronny said. “How much money you make a year?” BRONNY JAMES SNAPPED ON A FAN COURT SIDE TONIGHT 😭 “How much money you make a year?” LMFAOOOOOOOO #LakeShow — FADE (@FadeAwayMedia) November 9, 2026 It’s unclear what the Pistons fan said to spark such a reaction from Bronny, who isn’t known to lose his cool. The 22-year-old’s last notable interaction with a heckler involved him hilariously telling the individual their chain was fake . He has developed some thick skin over the years, but Lakers staffers had to restrain him here. Bronny, who is making $2.3 million in 2026-27, seemed to mock the fan’s weight with the “running a mile” comment and then delivered the typical athlete taunt about money. According to the video, the fan was later ejected from the game. This was the second time in three games that a fan was ejected from a Lakers game. item.title: “Just Lost His MVP Bid,” “Getting Carried by Defense”: NFL Fans React As Caleb Williams Throws 4 INTs in Bears’ Win vs. Buccaneers
item.description: Caleb Williams Bears © Imagn Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams struggled with multiple interceptions in Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite the quarterback’s disastrous night, the Bears pulled off a dramatic 27-24 victory. Williams threw a career-high four interceptions. The Bears signal-caller completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns. Williams’ interceptions allowed Tampa Bay to come back after trailing 17-6 at halftime. NFL fans reacted to Williams’ underwhelming performance in the Bears’ win. “Caleb Williams just lost his MVP bid,” one fan wrote. “Caleb Williams getting CARRIED by his defense,” another fan added. “It’s no way Caleb Williams can throw 4 picks, have his team still win, and be in MVP conversation. That’s being carried, which is the opposite of what MVP is,” one fan noted. “Once again showing Caleb Williams gets carried by his team..💀 unethical hooper,” one fan remarked. “Caleb Williams MVP stock dropping tonight,” one fan added. “Caleb Williams MVP talk should die after this. This team needs to be humble,” one fan commented. Many fan conversations focused on Williams hurting his MVP chances with his performance on Sunday. However, those hopes may be doomed for now after he threw four picks. According to USA Today , it was the first time in his career, including his time in college football, that he threw this many interceptions. Last season, he threw three interceptions in the game that ended last year’s NFC divisional-round loss to the Los Angeles Rams. He also had three interceptions in a loss to Notre Dame during his final season at USC. Caleb Williams Redeems Himself With Clutch Pass In Bucs Win Caleb Williams’ Chicago entered halftime with a 17-6 lead, but Tampa Bay’s second-half surge made things interesting. After Williams threw his fourth interception, Jaylon Johnson intercepted Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield and returned it 67 yards for a touchdown. Tampa Bay’s Bucky Irving responded with his second rushing touchdown with 2:51 remaining to tie the game at 24-24, also thanks to Mayfield’s two-point conversion. With the game potentially heading into overtime, Williams put the Bears in field goal range in Tampa Bay territory. He did so when he connected with tight end Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain. Chicago’s kicker Cairo Santos did the rest, hitting the game-winning 38-yard field goal to secure the Bears’ 27-24 win. As a result, Chicago improved to 7-2, while Tampa Bay dropped to 3-6. item.title: Most overrated/underrated teams in Week 10 coaches poll
item.description: After Week 10, we still don't quite know where the college football season will take us. What we do know though is that there may be more teams than ever in the reckoning for a top 12 CFP spot. Yet another No. 1 team has gone down, with Miami losing to Notre Dame on the road. Oh yeah, and Utah and UCLA remain the only undefeated teams in the country. Here are the most overrated and underrated teams in yet another crazy coaches poll. Overrated: No. 6 Miami Well, you kind of had to expect the fact that once Miami played a solid team, they may falter. That was the case yesterday as even a furious comeback couldn't lift the Hurricanes past a determined Notre Dame squad. Even though Darian Mensah threw three second half touchdown passes, sans Malachi Toney, he did not play a consistent game and looked rattled early in the matchup. For now, Miami shouldn't feel too bad about their CFP chances, but they must ensure that they win the ACC because there may not be margin for error for a two loss ACC runner up. Underrated: No. 4 UCLA Is UCLA really this good? They just might be. They many not have the best strength of schedule or of record, but they get the job done week in week out. Ever since Nico Iamaleava's injury, Ty Dieffenbach has played safe, efficient football. Yesterday though, it was his time to shine. On only 8 total completions, he had a total of 303 yards and three touchdowns. In fact, two of UCLA's drives were 75 yard dimes for Dieffenbach. Voters continue to underestimate the Bruins at their own peril. It's now not funny that they're continuing to be disregarded. This is the lowest they have been ranked this late in a season since then, and while there have been a lot of determining factors, this team looks nothing like a CFP contender, let alone a top 25 team. It feels weird considering that Luke Fahey really is not at fault, and yet is helpless to find a way to uplift this squad. Add in a frustrated Jeremiah Smith and a defense that looks wholly different than they did to start the season, and you get a very sticky situation in Columbus. Underrated: No. 23 South Carolina The resurgence of the Gamecocks is one that could see them be a point of contention amongst the committee by year's end. While they have three losses on their resume, they've been able to rebound in spirited fashion. item.title: ‘Morally bankrupt’: NFL criticized for chasing Taylor Swift fans as Josh Jacobs plays through abuse allegations
item.description: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The NFL has worked hard to grow its female fanbase in recent years, and Taylor Swift’s relationship with Travis Kelce has been a big part of that. But according to one columnist, the league is undermining all of that progress with how it has handled the situation regarding Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs. This week, Jacobs was back on the field for the Green Bay Packers despite new abuse allegations from three women, which surfaced just days after he returned from a six-game absence. In a new column, Daily Mail US deputy sports editor Rich Jones argued that the situation is “more proof the league is morally bankrupt.” Josh Jacobs’ Return Jacobs was arrested in May after an altercation with his then-girlfriend, who said he threw her to the ground. In September, he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property, and he spent the first six games of the season on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. Shortly after Jacobs returned, the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department released records from its investigation that included accounts from three other women describing similar allegations from previous years, according to NFL.com . item.title: LSU sweeps fall baseball doubleheader against Troy
item.description: Following a successful weekend in Biloxi, Jay Johnson’s Tigers returned home for a Sunday doubleheader. LSU welcomed in Troy for two 9-inning games. Although they lost a good amount of their impact players, the Trojans are coming off of an Omaha visit, making it to the College World Series for the first time in program history just 5 months ago. The Tigers took both games of the doubleheader in what was a beautiful day at the Box. It was a late inning comeback in game 1 with LSU down 9-5 in the 8th inning, but a 3-run homerun by their leader, Steven Milam, got them within striking distance for the 9th. Notre Dame transfer, Bino Watters, made his purple and gold debut this weekend and could not have gotten off to a better start. With two outs in the 9th, he walked it off with a 2-run single to clinch a 10-9 victory. LSU got a strong start by William Schmidt, with impressive relief appearances by Diego Velazquez and Lucas Nawrocki to bookend the game on the mound. Nawrocki has flashed his ability to be a 2-way player this fall and that was on display in this one, as he started at DH and went 1-2 with a triple at the plate, then pitched the final inning in which he struck out the side to eventually get credited with the win. The second game of the day was all Tigers from the very beginning. Last year’s ace, Casan Evans, made his second fall appearance and was dominant, striking out 5 in just 2.0 innings of work. Cooper Sides and Braxton Beaty followed him up by combining for 4 innings of no hit baseball, including 7 strikeouts. After a shaky outing from Kaden Smith, Ethan Plog took over to close out the game by also not allowing a hit and striking out 3. The offense got out to a hotter start in the second game than they did the first. That was in large part to Nawrocki, who led off with a solo homerun after closing out game 1 on the mound. Watters delivered 2 more hits, making it 5 total on the day. Jason Wachs, Dominic Santarelli, and Parker Loew each drove in runs later in the game, helping the Tigers complete the sweep with a 9-3 final score. Being a self-professed expert on the state of places I don’t actually go to, I have for years regarded Selhurst Park as one of the last bastions (at Premier League level) of the “real” game. An old fashioned stadium in the heart of the local community with what seems to be an energetic and noisy working class fan base. It certainly comes over that way on the TV and I always enjoy the passion and volume of the Palace fans. Despite their recent trophy successes – or maybe I should be saying BECAUSE of those successes – Palace are currently struggling in the Premier League. Midweek European games on top of season after season selling their best players has finally caught up with them, it would seem. Things have become so bad that they even contrived to lose at home …… to us! When reading the Palace fans’ post-match comments on The Mag. I was struck by two references in particular regarding the atmosphere. One referred to our supporters completely out-singing theirs and offering up the ditty, “shall we sing a song for you?” I must say, it was noticeable on the TV that our guys were consistently louder than theirs – something I don’t normally expect at Selhurst Park. In contrast with Darren Henderson’s assertion, in what I thought was an excellent article , ( ‘Newcastle United on the road to nowhere via Putney Bridge’ ) published on The Mag on Bonfire Night, that our away support has become “stagnant”, my ears confirmed that it was very much vibrant and in full flow at Selhurst Park on this occasion at least. Visitors to Selhurst Park will know that the popular end of the ground is the Holmsdale Road end and that Palace have a tradition of their most committed supporters gathering there and being orchestrated by a core group of “ultras” known as the Holmsdale Fanatics. Ultras are very much a European phenomenon – the hard core of the home support, inevitably dressed primarily in black and using a variety of aids, such as drums, megaphones, pyrotechnics and “choirmasters”, to increase noise levels and lead the support within the stadium. They are not generally associated with British teams. Indeed, new Palace manager Pierre Sage stated that a key reason he decided to take charge of the club is because it was one of the only clubs in the Premier League that had ultras. He didn’t mention salary …. The group was founded in December 2005 by a small number of supporters who had attended matches together since childhood in the 1980s. They traditionally stood in Block B of the Holmsdale Road Stand since 1999 but have had a bit of a running battle with the club, especially following stadium regulations introduced as a result of the Taylor report, which they described as restrictive. Longstanding supporters having to give up season tickets as referenced by Greg’s Chelsea supporting pals. Youngsters being priced out of match day and being replaced by “tourists” prepared to pay the commercial rates for a one-off experience. item.title: Pirates 2B Brandon Lowe among potential free agent busts
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 13: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates looks on during the seventh inning against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field on September 13, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Isaac Wasserman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe is a free agent this offseason, and the team could look to re-sign him or let him walk to another team on the open market. Lowe, 32, enjoyed a breakout year with the Pirates, where he had 5.3 wins above replacement, a career high for the 9-year veteran. In 150 appearances for the Pirates, he had a batting average of .260, 35 home runs, and 96 runs batted in. His strong showing in a contract year makes him one of the top free-agent infielders available, but that could be a flash in the pan. It’s very possible we may have seen the best of Lowe already. Bleacher Report contributor Zachary D. Rymer listed Lowe as one of the top eight potential free agent busts in the league this offseason. “The bad stuff concerns what happened when Lowe didn’t make contact. His 28.8 K% marked his highest strikeout rate since 2019, and it might undersell how much he swung and missed. He had a 66.9 contact percentage, third-lowest among qualified hitters,“ Rymer wrote. “That would be easy to forgive if Lowe had good plate discipline, but his 33.6 chase percentage was a career high and in the 27th percentile to boot. That’s never ideal, and least of all for a 32-year-old whose “old man skills” should be getting sharper.“ Lowe is expected to get many strong offers in free agency, which could poach him from the Pirates, who would love to re-sign him but at a reasonable price tag. Other teams may offer Lowe a much larger bag, which could mean he is one-and-done in Pittsburgh. These concerns might be part of the reason why the Pirates are hesitant to give him a larger deal, but they have their number in mind for him when negotiations begin in the offseason.

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. item.description: They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day. A fortnight in which they were defeated by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid , in which they might have wondered if something was not right, ended with a 2-1 win at Atlético Madrid. This was a proper test and a proper game, 10 World Cup winners on the field and first place awaiting the winner, and at the end of an intense enjoyable night, that was Hansi Flick’s side. At a noisy Metropolitano, the atmosphere matching the occasion, against a frenetic Atlético side that went for the throat, Barcelona trailed to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frenzied first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of the break leading them to the kind of victory that brings a reward beyond the points. It hadn’t been easy but they had made it; ultimately, they might conclude they had found a way to manage it too, some satisfaction in the suffering, in how they resisted and re-established control amid the chaos. In the first half we lost all the duels, all the contacts. Against this team, that is fighting relegation, if you don’t match them … it’s something we need to understand. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. item.description: The Super Falcons won’t be at the World Cup and with the prize money going up, they risk being left even further behind It was a historic result in Casablanca – but not in a good way. It is a crushing blow for the most decorated national side in Africa across both men and women, one that has won no fewer than 10 Wafcon titles . item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
